assumptions.text: n,N are arbitrary natural numbers. All scalar fields are real and all sphere metrics are induced from the real Euclidean inner product.
For the main identity, f:M->R is intrinsically C1 and each V_i:M->E is intrinsically C1.
Tangency holds pointwise: <x_i,V_i(x)>=0 for every configuration x and i.

For the weighted-gradient specialization, rho:M->R is intrinsically C1 and g:M->R is intrinsically C2. No sign or probability normalization of rho is necessary for this geometric identity. If rho is later interpreted as a density, its nonnegativity/normalization and the operator identification are separate application obligations.

boundaries.text: The measure is precisely normalized polar surface measure and its finite product. The theorem does not apply to arbitrary measures or to ambient volume restricted to the sphere.

No global ambient extension or its C1/C2 regularity is a source hypothesis. If an implementation proves only an ambient-extension theorem, it is an intermediate lemma: the intrinsic-to-extension bridge must still be proved before this contract is fulfilled.
Tangency, intrinsic test regularity and density regularity are substantive assumptions. No Sobolev/weak-regularity or nonsmooth-density extension is claimed.

This is a static geometric integral theorem. It does not construct a diffusion or density, justify differentiation in time of entropy, prove a generator-divergence identity for an unspecified model, or identify an arbitrary supplied measure/operator with the ones defined here.

Intrinsic gradient identification means the actual induced Euclidean tangent differential/Riesz pairing, not a named gradient placeholder. The tangent trace must agree with intrinsic divergence under the derived local regularity.

definitions.text: n,N range over Nat, E=Euclidean R^(n+1), S=unit sphere, M={x:Fin N->S}. N=0 is allowed: the product is a point, all coordinate sums are empty and the identities are zero=zero. n=0 is also allowed: S is the two-point zero-dimensional sphere. There is no positive-dimension restriction hidden in a truncated dimension subtraction.

tau=(Lebesgue measure on E).toSphere, the polar measure on S. Its total mass is finite and strictly positive because dim(E)=n+1>0. sigma=tau(S)^(-1) tau, with inverse in the nonnegative extended reals and scalar multiplication of measures. The product measure is the finite measure product over i in Fin N. It is an actual probability measure; no arbitrary measure sigma is supplied.

For any sphere function h with codomain R or E, define its canonical radial extension h^r on E by h^r(z)=h(z/||z||) when z!=0 and h^r(0)=0. The value at zero is merely a total-function convention. Every derivative defining a sphere operator is taken at a unit vector inside the open nonzero region. No differentiability or continuity at zero is required or implied.

For x in S, P_x is the actual orthogonal projection onto x-perp: P_x v=v-<v,x>x. Define grad_S h(x)=P_x grad_E(h^r)(x). For W:S->E define div_S W(x)=div_E(W^r)(x), where div_E is the coordinate trace of the Frechet derivative. Under C1 regularity the first operator is the ordinary intrinsic gradient; the second is the ordinary intrinsic divergence when W is tangent; proving their tangent-differential/trace identification is part of the required bridge, not a new assumption.

For x in M, write x[i<-y] for configuration x with coordinate i replaced by y. Define grad_i f(x)=grad_S(y->f(x[i<-y]))(x_i), and div_M V(x)=sum_i div_S(y->V_i(x[i<-y]))(x_i). Pairings are sum_i<grad_i f(x),V_i(x)> with no factor 1/N. This is the product Riemannian operator and normalization.

Intrinsically Ck means Ck in the ordinary stereographic charts on S and finite product charts on M. The vector field components are Ck maps from M to the ambient Euclidean E, with pointwise tangency. No globally Ck ambient extension is supplied; canonical radial regularity away from the zero coordinates must be derived from these intrinsic hypotheses.

formulae.text: div_M V, f div_M V and sum_i<grad_i f,V_i> are integrable. The corresponding weighted-specialization integrands are also integrable. All identities are ordinary finite real integrals; none is an a.e.-in-time statement.

proof_inventory.detail: Use the smooth radial normalization on E minus {0}, the stereographic sphere charts and product charts to derive C1 or C2 regularity of the canonical extension wherever every coordinate is nonzero. Establish extension agreement on S, tangent differentiation, the radial derivative zero identity, and identification with the induced metric operators. The artificial zero value at the origin is never used as a differentiability premise.

Multiply the radial extension of a tangent field by a smooth scalar radial cutoff supported in a positive annulus. This produces a globally C1 compactly supported ambient field as an internal construction. Apply the existing whole-space zero-divergence producer, and the existing Haar-to-sphere polar decomposition. Tangency kills the derivative of the radial cutoff. The remaining radial factor is integral chi(r)/r * r^n dr; choose it nonzero and cancel it. No new proof of the ambient divergence theorem or ball-flux theorem is needed.
proof_inventory.move: Zero integral of single-sphere tangential divergence

proof_inventory.detail: Derive the actual tangent product rule div_S(fW)=<grad_S f,W>+f div_S W using the canonical radial derivatives and existing orthogonal-projection identities. Apply P2 to fW. Compactness and intrinsic regularity derive integrability; no IBP identity is assumed.

Scale both sides by the explicit reciprocal polar surface mass, identify sigma exactly, and apply single-sphere identities to coordinate sections. Joint intrinsic C1 regularity gives continuous section derivatives and integrability on the compact product. Finite-product Fubini and finite summation yield F1-F2 with no 1/N factor, including the empty product.

Derive joint C1 regularity and tangency of rho grad_i g from intrinsic C1 rho and C2 g, via the full product radial extension and parameter-dependent derivative calculus. Substitute this actual vector field in F1-F2 and use finite scalar-inner-product algebra to obtain F3-F4.

statement: Let n,N be arbitrary natural numbers, E=R^(n+1), S={x in E:||x||=1}, and M=S^N. Equip S with the normalized polar surface measure sigma obtained from Euclidean Lebesgue measure, and M with sigma^N. Give S its usual induced Euclidean Riemannian metric and stereographic smooth structure and M their product structures. For every intrinsically C1 real function f on M and every intrinsically C1 vector field V=(V_i) taking V_i(x) in the actual tangent hyperplane x_i-perp, the integral of div_M V is zero and integral_M f div_M V = -integral_M sum_i <grad_i f,V_i>. The integrands are integrable. The divergence and gradients are the actual local differential operators, specified below through the canonical radial extension; no extension regularity or integral identity is an input. In particular, for C1 real rho and C2 real g on M, the same formula applies to V_i=rho grad_i g and yields weighted gradient integration by parts and zero integral of its divergence.
title: Tangential divergence and integration by parts on finite products of unit spheres
